summary: You developed a compelling mission concept for Great Barrier Reef monitoring using fluid lensing, with clear stakeholder identification and effective STK simulations. Your introduction and conclusion successfully frame the mission requirements. To reach higher marks, focus on technical accuracy in orbital mechanics (specifically launch physics and RAAN definition), clean up duplicate STK access data and incomplete sentences, and adopt professional reporting standards by replacing Wikipedia references and adding formal captions to all figures and tables.
next_steps: Correct core orbital mechanics concepts: revise the launch physics to account for Earth's rotational penalty on retrograde SSO orbits, and correctly define RAAN as an inertial celestial reference rather than terrestrial launch longitude.
Proofread and verify simulated data: eliminate duplicate entries in your Ground Control STK access table (rows 14 and 15) and complete the truncated sentence in your Mission Duration & EOL section.

Professionalise report presentation: format all figures and tables with standard numbering and captions, remove raw pasted web tables, and replace Wikipedia citations with authoritative technical sources.

criteria.C1: You articulated an excellent, well-rationalised mission concept in the Introduction, clearly justifying a single spacecraft for coral reef monitoring and identifying operators like CSIRO and BOM. To reach the top mark, continue backing operational assumptions with deeper literature references.
criteria.C2: You addressed the required design elements using STK effectively. To achieve Accomplished, ensure your technical explanations are accurate: equatorial rotation penalises retrograde Sun-synchronous orbits rather than boosting them, and RAAN is an inertial reference, not launch longitude. Also, resolve duplicate entries in the STK access table and finish the truncated sentence in your EOL discussion.
criteria.C3: Your conclusion neatly synthesised your major mission decisions, linking the Vega E launcher, orbital regime, and ground station capability directly back to reef monitoring goals. To strengthen it further, you could briefly highlight key trade-offs and suggest specific operational contingency plans if launch vehicle availability shifts.
criteria.C4: You maintained a logical structure with clear headings. To progress to Accomplished, assign formal captions and numbers (e.g., Table 1, Figure 1) to all graphics and tables. Avoid pasting raw web tables with unformatted footnote brackets, and replace non-academic sources like Wikipedia with primary technical literature or launch manifest documentation.
